title: AI SEO: how to get your content cited by ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overviews
summary: Corey Haines' open-source AI SEO playbook for getting cited by AI assistants. It layers extractable structure, citable authority and third-party presence on top of normal SEO, and covers agent-readable pricing files, the citation vs recommendation gap, and measuring non-deterministic AI answers with repeated runs.

principles.text: Treat AI SEO as a layer on top of traditional SEO, not a replacement for it.
principles.quote: Strong organic rankings are still one of the best predictors of AI visibility, so treat structure as a layer on top of SEO, not a replacement.

principles.text: Write extractable content: every key claim should stand alone as a passage AI can lift.
principles.quote: AI systems extract passages, not pages. Every key claim should work as a standalone statement.

principles.text: Add sourced stats and citations to boost AI visibility; keyword stuffing actively hurts it.
principles.quote: keyword stuffing actively reduces AI visibility by 10% (Princeton GEO study)

principles.text: Make pricing machine-readable, or AI agents buying on a user's behalf will skip you for competitors.
principles.quote: If your pricing is locked in a JavaScript-rendered page or a "contact sales" wall, agents will skip you and recommend competitors whose information they can actually read.

principles.text: Being cited is not being recommended; shortlists depend on what third parties say about you.
principles.quote: Shortlist recommendations lean on what reviews, forums, and press say about you, even where your own site earns most citations

principles.text: Measure AI visibility with repeated runs and mention rates, never a single answer.
principles.quote: one run is an anecdote, not a measurement.
